diagnostic_evidence.quote: we call the first \(N_{S}\) DoFs \(\mathscr{S}\)-identifiying, if: \(\forall \boldsymbol{p}\in \mathscr{S}\ \left\{\mathcal{F}_{1}\left(\boldsymbol{p}\right)=\dots=\mathcal{F}_{N_{S}}\left(\boldsymbol{p}\right)=0\right\} \implies \boldsymbol{p}=0\).

issues.failure_explanation: The claim asserts that the L2 projection Π^S of v onto S is determined by the first N_S DoFs of v. S-identifiability (injectivity of D_NS on S) does not imply this: the map v ↦ (v,p)_K for p in S need not factor through D_NS(v). Concretely, with V = P_1 on the unit disk, S = P_0, and DoFs F_1=v(0), F_2=∫v, F_3=∫xv, F_1 alone identifies S but Π^S v = (∫v)/π is not a function of F_1(v). Without the missing hypothesis (moments against S determined by preserved DoFs) the construction 'V^S with these DoFs' need not have dimension N_S or admit the preserved DoFs as a DoF set.

failure_location.quote: Note that the projection can be solely determined by \(\left\{\mathcal{F}_{i}\right\},i=1,\dots,N_{S}\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Definition defvs the hypothesis that (v,p)_K for p in S factors as D_NS(v)^T G D_NS(p) for a symmetric positive definite G (equivalently, that Π^S v is determined by D_NS(v)), and record that this hypothesis is verified for each concrete space via the propcompoly argument.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract justification that the preserved DoFs form a DoF set for V^S is unsupported in general. In the concrete VEM instantiations the property holds via integration-by-parts/polynomial-decomposition arguments of the propcompoly type, so the specific constructions and downstream theorems for the face/edge/node spaces remain valid there.
issues.title: Serendipity projection claimed determined by preserved DoFs without justification
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis preserves every substantive claim and guarantee for the concrete VEM spaces where the property is verified; no new nontrivial lemma or construction is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis v ∈ H^s(K) implies only ∇v ∈ H^{s-1}(K), so the seminorm |∇v|_{s,K} on the right-hand side is infinite for generic v in the stated class. Either the hypothesis must be strengthened to v ∈ H^{s+1}(K) (which at the top of the stated range s=m+1 demands an unattainable rate for a P_m-conforming method) or the estimate must be restated as h_K^{s-1}|∇v|_{s-1,K} = h_K^{s-1}|v|_{s,K} (which gives the optimal h_K^m|v|_{m+1,K} at s=m+1). The two repairs are mathematically different, so the correction is not a forced single edit.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the estimate as ‖∇(v - I^Sn_h v)‖_K ≲ h_K^{s-1}|∇v|_{s-1,K} for v ∈ H^s(K), 3/2 < s ≤ m+1 (equivalently h_K^{s-1}|v|_{s,K}); alternatively keep h_K^s|∇v|_{s,K} but require v ∈ H^{s+1}(K) and restrict s ≤ m so the rate is attainable.
issues.overall_effect: As written the theorem's estimate is vacuous (RHS infinite) on its stated hypothesis class, so the advertised optimal gradient-approximation property of the node serendipity space is not established at the claimed regularity range.
issues.title: Node-space interpolation estimate has hypothesis/regularity mismatch
issues.why_classification: Both candidate repairs are local index shifts on a single displayed estimate that preserve the method, conclusion, optimal rate and scope with no new nontrivial lemma, construction or replacement argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The one-line proof reduces the claim to thmve applied to ∇v. Thmve is stated for edge spaces V^Se_{β,k_d,μ_r} with β=(m,β_d,m-1), m=[s], and P^3_m ⊆ V^Se. The natural edge space containing ∇V^Sn_{m,k_f,k_v} has β=(m-1,k_f,-1); matching β=(m',β_d,m'-1) forces m'-1=-1 hence m'=0 and m=1. For m>1 the hypotheses of thmve are not met (β_r=-1 ≠ m'-1, and the curl-free edge space does not contain P^3_{m-1} which includes non-curl-free vector polynomials), so the reduction does not go through. Enlarging the ambient edge space to a V^Se with P^3_{m'} contained requires separately verifying that ∇V^Sn actually lies in that V^S (the reduced-DoF constraints F_i(v)=F_i(Π^S v) are face/surface pairings and are not automatically satisfied by the L^2-orthogonality defining Π^S).

failure_location.quote: The assertion simply follows from \(\left[3\right]\) in \cref{eqcomm} and and \cref{thmve}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a variant of thmve covering the edge space of gradients of V^Sn (equivalently, edge spaces with β_r = -1 and S = ∇P_m rather than P^3_m) with the analogous reduced-DoF moment argument, verifying the containment ∇V^Sn ⊆ V^S explicitly; alternatively prove thm:added-1 directly via eqcomm [3] and a bespoke interpolation estimate for the edge space of gradients.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:added-1 is unproved for polynomial degree m>1; the advertised general-order optimal gradient approximation for the node serendipity space is unsupported beyond the lowest order, and the exact-sequence commuting property used downstream in the method is correspondingly unverified in that regime.
issues.title: Node-space interpolation proof applies thmve outside its stated hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The current one-line proof is invalid beyond the lowest order; a contained nontrivial generalization of thmve (or a direct argument) is needed, but the statement and its optimal rate survive without new global proof architecture or major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the Lagrange bases are linear independent, there must be some \(l\) making \(\mathbf{M}^l\) full row rank.
As \(\left\|\bm{\mathit{\Pi}}_{l}\boldsymbol{\psi}^l_{i}\right\|\) monotonically increases with \(l\), it must converges as \(l\rightarrow\infty\).

issues.failure_explanation: The proof names an object ψ^∞_i that is never defined (only the scalar sequence ‖Π_l ψ^l_i‖ is shown bounded and increasing); the asserted identity ‖Π ψ^∞_i‖ = ‖ψ^∞_i‖ 'by density of polynomials' is either trivially true (if Π is the identity on L^2 closure of polynomials) or meaningless. The claimed monotonicity of ‖Π_l ψ^l_i‖ in l presupposes ψ^l_i is independent of l, which itself requires the unproved earlier claim in defvs that moments against polynomials are determined by the preserved DoFs. Finally, the passage from 'Lagrange bases are linearly independent' to 'there is some l with M^l full row rank' skips the necessary argument that the truncated Gram matrix (M^l)(M^l)^T converges to the positive-definite L^2 Gram matrix of the {ψ_i} and hence is positive definite for large l — the step that actually turns ‖Π_l ·‖ into a norm on V^S_l.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the proof to: (i) show that (ψ_i, m_j) is independent of l because moments against polynomials are determined by the preserved DoFs (via the propcompoly-style argument, i.e. the hypothesis of ISSUE-001); (ii) apply Parseval to identify lim_{l→∞} ‖Π_l ψ_i‖^2 = Σ_j (ψ_i,m_j)^2 = ‖ψ_i‖^2 (replacing the ill-defined ψ^∞_i step); and (iii) show M^l has full row rank for large l by noting (M^l)(M^l)^T converges to the positive-definite Gram matrix of the L^2-independent {ψ_i} (hence is positive definite for large l by continuity), which makes v ↦ ‖Π_l v‖ a norm on V^S_l and yields the equivalence via finite-dimensional norm equivalence.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:added-2 (existence of l with ‖Π_l v‖ ≈ ‖v‖ on V^S_l) is unproved as written; the stabilization-free guarantee and the subsequent 'equivalent discrete bilinear form' construction rest on this unestablished stability, so the paper's central claim is unsupported until the argument is supplied.
issues.title: Existence-of-stable-projection proof uses undefined limits and non-sequitur rank argument
issues.why_classification: The proof as written contains undefined objects and unjustified inferences, so a substantive rewrite is required; however the underlying strategy (moment matrix + Parseval + Gram-matrix positive-definiteness) is available and yields the same statement and rate without new global proof architecture or loss of the main guarantee.
